security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences, JavaScript template literals, relative documentation links, and public example URLs. One example fetches an unvalidated caller-provided URL, which can enable server-side request forgery in server rendering contexts. The voiceover example also constructs an output path from unvalidated identifiers.

remediation.issue: Caller-provided dataUrl is fetched without destination validation.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only HTTPS URLs from approved hosts, reject private and loopback addresses, and enforce request timeouts and response-size limits before fetching.

remediation.issue: Voiceover output paths interpolate compositionId and scene.id.
remediation.suggestion: Validate identifiers against a restrictive filename allowlist, resolve the target path, and reject paths outside the intended public/voiceover directory.

remediation.issue: Examples reference remote media and third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should review remote asset origins and provide their own approved URLs and service credentials.

content.value_statement: Building video compositions can require many React, timing, and media decisions. This skill provides focused Remotion patterns for creating maintainable video markup.
actual_capabilities: Explains React markup patterns for Remotion compositions.
Guides animation timing with frames, interpolation, easing, and springs.
Shows how to add video, audio, images, GIFs, and Lottie assets.
Covers sequencing, trimming, transitions, captions, and visual effects.
Describes calculateMetadata for dynamic duration, dimensions, and props.
Provides mapping, fonts, text measurement, and voiceover guidance.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a renderer or project generator.
Remote media, maps, and TTS services need user-managed access and credentials.
It does not validate URLs, asset paths, or third-party service responses for a production deployment.
Output quality still depends on the project assets, composition design, and Remotion version.

use_cases.title: Create a product video
use_cases.description: Build a React composition with animated text, images, audio, and scene timing.

use_cases.title: Edit a video timeline
use_cases.description: Trim clips, sequence scenes, and calculate duration for a multi-part composition.

use_cases.title: Add narrated explainers
use_cases.description: Generate scene audio with an approved TTS provider and match composition length to audio.

prompt_templates.title: Start a composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple Remotion composition with a title, background color, and fade-in animation.

prompt_templates.title: Add media assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Add an image sequence and background audio to my Remotion composition. Use local public assets and explain the timing.

prompt_templates.title: Build a scene timeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me sequence three video scenes with trims, overlaps, and a transition at 30 frames per second.

prompt_templates.title: Design dynamic metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a calculateMetadata function for my Remotion composition. Validate external URLs and keep all fetched data within approved limits.

output_examples.input: Create a title card that appears during the first second.
output: A composition outline with a full-frame title card.
Frame-based opacity and scale timing guidance.

output_examples.input: Make my composition match the duration of an audio file.
output: A calculateMetadata approach for measuring audio duration.
A frame-duration calculation using the selected FPS.
A note to validate asset locations before rendering.
A map composition structure using a reviewed style source.
Notes about network access and asset ownership.

best_practices: Use local or approved media assets when rendering production videos.
Keep timing calculations in frames and define the composition FPS clearly.
Validate external URLs and dynamic asset identifiers before server-side rendering.
anti_patterns: Do not place unvalidated user identifiers directly into output file paths.
Do not fetch arbitrary user-provided URLs from a rendering server.
Do not depend on remote media without considering availability, licensing, and caching.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you create Remotion video compositions with React, media, animation, and timing patterns.

faq.question: Does it render videos for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance for a Remotion project that you render with your own tools.

faq.question: Can I use remote media URLs?
faq.answer: Yes, but review the source, availability, licensing, and security controls before production use.

faq.question: Does it support dynamic composition duration?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents calculateMetadata patterns for duration, dimensions, and transformed props.

faq.question: Can it help with voiceovers?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes a TTS workflow, but you must manage provider credentials and validate generated output paths.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
